slides.title: Handling Player Input 🎮

quizData.question: Input Actions and Axis Mappings must be defined in Project Settings before binding in C++.
quizData.explanation: The bindings refer to action/axis names that must match those in Project Settings or Enhanced Input assets.

slides.title: Spawning Actors 🌱
slides.content:
## Create at Runtime

To spawn an actor:
```cpp
AActor* Spawned = GetWorld()->SpawnActor<AMyActor>(AMyActor::StaticClass(), SpawnLocation, SpawnRotation);
```
* `GetWorld()` returns the current world (only valid after BeginPlay).
* `SpawnActor` needs the class, location, and rotation.
* Optionally use `SpawnParameters` to set owner, instigator, etc.

You can also spawn from a Blueprint class:
```cpp
UClass* BPClass = LoadClass<AMyActor>(nullptr, TEXT("/Game/Blueprints/BP_MyActor.BP_MyActor_C"));
GetWorld()->SpawnActor<AMyActor>(BPClass, ...);
```

slides.title: Timers in C++ ⏱️
slides.content:
## Schedule Functions

Use `SetTimer` to call a function after a delay:
```cpp
FTimerHandle TimerHandle;
GetWorldTimerManager().SetTimer(TimerHandle, this, &AMyActor::MyFunction, 2.0f, false);
```
* `TimerHandle` – identifier to clear the timer later.
* `this` – the object on which to call.
* `&AMyActor::MyFunction` – pointer to member function.
* `2.0f` – delay.
* `false` – not looping; `true` to loop.

To clear: `GetWorldTimerManager().ClearTimer(TimerHandle);`

This is the C++ equivalent of the Blueprint Set Timer node.

quizData.question: To manage timers, you need a _____ variable to reference the timer.
quizData.explanation: FTimerHandle uniquely identifies a timer, allowing you to clear or pause it.

slides.title: Line Traces 🔍
Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Draw Debug Line

During development, use `DrawDebugLine(GetWorld(), Start, End, FColor::Red, false, 2.0f);` to visualise your traces.
